checks: An affine constituent vanishing at a sampled point has nonzero continuous slope; otherwise the whole sampled fiber would have zero parameter. The level cut keeps fixed inballs for small height, preserves anchored compatibility, removes positive volume tending to zero and gives a log deficit at least a_t times |log t|.

Absolute continuity of the given integrable log yields h_t tending to zero and a_t=o(h_t). The positive upper bound for log L controls any second removed set without requiring that its inverse density or log be uniformly bounded below.

The cut-family hinge normalization uses positive limiting surface costs. Integrating the surface areas of the actual inner parallel bodies gives uniform first losses along s_t=C_0a_t and leaves every old atomic covering cap strictly below the original normalized ratio.

The final normalization is the exact sum of the two removed log integrals divided by the final mass. Nested energy monotonicity and O(a_t) mass/covariance changes leave a uniform order-h_t decrease in the physical shift on retained marks.

A compact old interior neighborhood with a strict atomic gap has uniform proper coarea and a positive original shift. The old caps lose order h_t before restriction to the final bodies. Other old gaps remain by nesting and smaller shifts, and division by the final mass costs only O(a_t). The case of no atomic caps is covered.

Every affine constituent is nonnegative on the hull. A zero of their finite minimum on the hull would therefore require one constituent to vanish on a sampled point, contradicting the previous argument.
